text:
The Wild arrive in Toronto with points in nine straight (7-0-2) and a 2-1 overtime win at MTL two days ago, which Kirill Kaprizov finished. The Maple Leafs are winless in four (0-4-0) after a 6-3 home loss to COL, and they're missing Kirill Marchenko, Colton Sissons and Nick Blankenburg. Morgan Rielly is day-to-day and could return. With Marchenko out, John Tavares has moved beside Paul and Nylander, and Jack Roslovic is up to 18:36 a night.

Minnesota has the better underlying numbers. At five on five, the Wild have taken 53% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in their games, to Toronto's 46%. Our model has MIN scoring 3.46 goals tonight to TOR's 2.73. Toronto also takes 4.3 penalties a game, and Minnesota's power play creates 0.92 expected goals a game.

In net, projected starter Jesper Wallstedt is 15.9 goals saved above expected this season, meaning he has stopped that many more than the shots deserved. Sergei Bobrovsky, also projected, is at -1.3 and has gone 0-5-0 over his last five starts.

Kaprizov (49% to score) and Matt Boldy (41%) lead our list for Minnesota; Auston Matthews is at 36% for Toronto. Our under-the-radar pick is Bobby Brink, a third-liner with 2.9 expected goals over his last 10 games. We have him at 18% to score and 40% for a point.
